newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises sharply on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises sharply on rate cut.

text.p: The Israeli shekel rose sharply on Monday against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies in active trading despite the interest rate cut announced in the morning, dealers said.
The Bank of Israel announced it was cutting the short-term base interest rate 0.3 percentage point to 15.2 percent.

"The dollar opened at 3.28 shekels, but it fell sharply because of the moderate cut. When the dollar reached 3.235 shekels investors used the opportunity to start buying dollars," said Gideon Sadeh at Bank Leumi. "Trading was very active."
"Despite the fact that the market was expecting a rate cut of only 0.3-0.5 percentage point, the actual decision was very disappointing," he said.

A trader at First International Bank said he doubted the dollar would come under long-term pressure because towards year-end many business would be repaying foreign currency loans and need to buy dollars.
"What we had 2-3 months ago when we went to nearly 7.0 percent (below the mid-range of the official currency band) in the basket, we won't see that again," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2550 shekels against 3.2810 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.6420 shekels against 3.6692 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8489 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8970 on Friday and against the mark at 2.1370 shekels against 2.1532.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2570 shekels.
